gaps.name: The cap's 3-path sample misses the real worst case by 3x, so the response is not bounded under the 10,000-byte line
gaps.reason: behavior wrong - the header's bounding claim does not hold on real paths; the maximality measurement was taken on a sample that excludes every path near the worst case
gaps.evidence: cadence-core/bin/lib/why-render.mjs:32-60. The header states the cap's job as bounding the response against the 10,000-byte line references/conventions.md sets (`the response is bounded by TRUNCATING THE ENTRY COUNT`), then measures three paths - lib/capture-file.mjs, lib/issue-decision.mjs, planning.mjs - and claims 6 is the largest cap under which `the worst of those paths` stays under the line. Swept 400 tracked paths at the shipped default: 47 of 400 render at or over 10,000 B. Worst is cadence-core/bin/why-record.test.mjs at 29,378 B (shown 6 of total 6, only 1 excluded, so it is join-field bytes and not the new exclusion block), then lib/why-record.mjs 28,044 B, lib/branch-decision.mjs 22,458 B, lib/deferred-reads.mjs 21,583 B, cadence-core/bin/deferred-reads.test.mjs 20,678 B. lib/why-render.mjs's own history renders 18,137 B. This is not a regression the phase introduced - the shipped cap of 10 was worse - but it is the same class of defect WHY-03 named: a byte claim whose sample does not reach the case it is being made about. A reader of the header concludes the render stays under the line; on 12% of sampled paths it does not, by up to 3.2x.
gaps.missing: Either widen the measurement to the worst path the sweep finds and restate the header's claim on it (a cap that holds cadence-core/bin/why-record.test.mjs under 10,000 B is 1-2 entries, which is likely unacceptable and is itself the finding), or state explicitly in the header that the cap bounds ENTRY COUNT and not bytes, that per-entry join bytes are unbounded, and name the measured range across paths rather than three samples. Do not leave a global-sounding bounding sentence sitting above a three-path table.
